claim: Rome's 2026 Michelin Guide lists 1 three-star (La Pergola) and 3 two-star restaurants (Il Pagliaccio, Acquolina, Enoteca La Torre).
quote: La Pergola, Anthony Genovese at Il Pagliaccio, Daniele Lippi at Acquolina, and Domenico Stile at Enoteca La Torre at Villa Laetitia hold two Michelin stars.

claim: La Pergola is the first and only three-Michelin-star restaurant in Rome, located at the Rome Cavalieri Waldorf Astoria hotel with panoramic views over the city.
quote: the first and, still today, the only three-star Michelin in Rome

claim: La Pergola reopened June 2024 after renovation; tasting menus are €350 (10 courses) and €290 (7 courses); kitchen added photovoltaic panels and induction cookers.
quote: Tasting menu options include: 10-course tasting: €350; 7-course tasting: €290

claim: Weekend reservations at La Pergola may require booking three months in advance; walk-ins are not possible.
quote: weekend reservations may need to be booked three months in advance. Walk-ins are essentially out of the question

claim: Il Pagliaccio offers four tasting menus: CIRCUS (9 courses, €270), SCINTILLE (6 courses, €230), INTERMEZZO (4 courses, €180), and PARALLELS EXPERIENCE (10 courses, €330, private room).
quote: CIRCUS: 9 courses €270 | SCINTILLE: 6 courses €230 | INTERMEZZO: 4 courses €180 | PARALLELS EXPERIENCE: 10 courses €330

claim: Il Pagliaccio features chic minimalist design; Chef Genovese founded it in 2003 and earned 2 stars within a few years with cuisine blending East-to-West influences.
quote: chic, modern, minimalist design with colorful accents throughout... a journey spanning from East to West, crossing the Mediterranean

claim: Acquolina is located at Via del Vantaggio 14, The First Roma Arte Hotel; accepts only online reservations; phone +39 063201590.
quote: Via del Vantaggio 14, 00186 Rome | Only online reservations accepted

claim: Daniele Lippi's cuisine is Mediterranean-focused; signature dishes include langoustines with kiwi and roe, spaghetti with citrus and sea urchins; kitchen brigade mostly under 30.
quote: Langoustines with kiwi, roe, tarragon oil | Spaghetti with citrus and sea urchins | 1,000-label wine cellar emphasizing small producers

claim: Acquolina tasting menus: Periplo (seafood-focused) €240, Anabasi Catabasi (includes meat) €280.
quote: Periplo - €240 per guest | Anabasi Catabasi - €280 per guest

claim: Enoteca La Torre is at Lungotevere delle Armi 23, open Wed–Sun; phone +39 06 4566 8304; won Best Wine Cellar in Italy 2022 (Le Guide de l'Espresso).
quote: Open Wednesday through Sunday for lunch and dinner service | Best Wine Cellar in Italy 2022

claim: Chef Domenico Stile trained under Massimo Bottura and Grant Achatz; the restaurant is inside Villa Laetitia (owned by Anna Fendi Venturini), an art-filled historic building.
quote: trained under renowned culinary masters including Massimo Bottura and Grant Achatz... Villa Laetitia (owned by Anna Fendi Venturini)

claim: Enoteca La Torre tasting menus: Menu Remuage €260, 'A Journey with Eyes Closed' €230; à la carte ~€200/person.
quote: Menu Remuage - €260 per guest | A Journey with eyes closed (2016/2026) - €230 per guest
